title: R' Chunya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 3:2 as mentioning him in a report in the name of R' Shmuel bar Nachman. In Bereshit Rabbah 98:5: R' Chunya and R' Azaryah in the name of R' Yochanan. In Shir HaShirim Rabbah, supplied locator פ״ד פ״ח-ב, in the name of Rabbi Yusta. In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14:3: Rabbi Chunya Yaakov of Ofratayim in the name of Rabbi. In Midrash Tehillim 2:16: R' Chunya in the name of Rav Idi.

It appears to Hyman that he is R' Huna, as in Bereshit Rabbah 1:14: “R' Chunya in the name of Rabbi”; this statement in Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1, folio 2b, reads “R' Chunah in the name of Rabbi.” In Tanchuma, Bamidbar 10, “R' Chunya,” and this statement is cited in the Yalkut there in the name of R' Huna. Likewise in Midrash Rabbah (מ״ר) 13:2, “R' Chunya,” and Esther Rabbah 2:14 reads R' Huna.

The earlier notes describe the evidence then available. The report of Chunya in the name of Rabbi Yusta occurs at Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8:2 in the consulted edition and in Tamar Kadari’s transcription of Vatican Hebrew MS 76. Hyman’s printed locator remains in the translation. The Guggenheimer text of Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 3:2 places Rabbi Yaakov bar Avun between Chunya and the reference to Shmuel bar Nachman. In Shabbat 14:3 the juxtaposition Chunya Yaakov of Ofratayim remains as written. The consulted Midrash Tehillim text (chapter 2) reads Rabbi Huna in the name of R’ Idi where Hyman records R’ Chunya in the name of Rav Idi.

Bereshit Rabbah 1:14 has Chunya in Rabbi’s name, and the parallel in Jerusalem Talmud Peah 1:1 has Chunah. Buber’s Tanchuma, Bamidbar 10, names Chunya in the teaching about pointing to a king’s image, while the consulted Yalkut Shimoni (Torah §684) gives Huna in parentheses and Chananya in brackets. Bamidbar Rabbah 13:2 and Esther Rabbah 2:14 contain the teaching about the north and south winds, attributed respectively to Rabbi Chunya and Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Binyamin bar Levi. The supplied Hebrew includes the words Mishlei Rabbah beside מ״ר, which Hyman’s printed page leaves abbreviated. The consulted Buber Midrash Mishlei 13:2 treats a different subject. The identification with Huna remains Hyman’s suggestion.
